Q: How to set different environment variables for each managed host in ansible A:

Please see the ansible documentation for this as it's rather explanatory: https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/user_guide/intro_inventory.html

I am editing my initial answer and try to make it more clear. But please note that I am assuming a few things here:

  1. you are using Linux
  2. you use bash as your shell, Linux offers a variety of shells and the syntax is different
  3. when you say export environment variables I assume you mean copy the variables to the remote host in some form and export them to the shell

Also there's a few things left to do but I have to leave it to you:

  • You need to "load" the env file so the variables are available to the shell (export), you can add an extra line to the ".bashrc" file to source the file, like "source /etc/env_variables", but that will depend on how you want to use the vars. You can easily do that with your shell script or with ansible (lineinfile)

  • I recommend you use a separate file like I did and don't edit the bashrc adding all the variables. It will make you life easier in the future if you want to update the variables.

  • Rename the env file properly so you know what's for and add some backup mechanism - check the documentation https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/blockinfile_module.html

Inventory file with the variables:

all:
  hosts:
    <your_host_name1>:
      sys: abc1
      cap: rty2
      jam: yup4
      pak: hyd4
      jum: 563
    <your_host_name2>:
      sys: abc45
      cap: hju
      jam: upy
      pak: upsc
      jum: y78

My very simplistic playbook:

- hosts: all
  become: yes
  become_method: sudo

  tasks:

    -  name: Create env file and add variables
       blockinfile:
         path: /etc/env_variables
         create: yes
         block: |
           export sys={{ sys }}
           export cap={{ cap }}
           export jam={{ jam }}
           export pak={{ pak }}
           export jum={{ jum }}

The final result on the servers I used for testing is the following:

server1:
# BEGIN ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK
export sys=abc1
export cap=rty2
export jam=yup4
export pak=hyd4
export jum=563
# END ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK

server2:
# BEGIN ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK
export sys=abc45
export cap=hju
export jam=upy
export pak=upsc
export jum=y78
# END ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK

Hope this is what you are asking for. For windows you may have to find where the user variables are set and adjust the playbook to edit that file, if they are in a text file...

Q: SQL query - regex pattern for all alphabets A:

make use of REGEXP and [:alpha] in your query something like

UPDATE dbo.Employee SET Sal = REPLACE(REPLACE(Sal,'-',''), ':', '')     
             WHERE Sal LIKE '%:%' OR Sal LIKE '%-%' OR Sal REGEXP '[:alpha]';

Q: Forcing "date" to use a locale other than the machine default A:

Change your locale

Set LC_ALL="fr_FR.utf-8" so you can have a french display (or whatever locale you want). This will change the language used by date, but not the timezone.

Change the timezone

Use the TZ (timezone) variable

So, something like :
TZ="Europe/Paris" date

Gives Paris time.

You can add export TZ="Europe/Paris" in your .profile to make it true for every session.

The tool tzselect can help you choose the correct string to put inside TZ. It basically prompts for the continent, the country and the city. It could also by used inside scripts to change the timezone based on user input.

Q: Claude OPUS and Concurrency in C++? A:

AI chatbots are not perfect at analysing multithreading C++ code. That shouldn't be a surprise. They aren't even good at it.

If you already included all the necessary code in the prompt and you got false replies, there is nothing you can do about it. Suppose you'd change your prompting and get a different result, this wouldn't (/shouldn't) increase your trust, because you already know it can give false replies.

Don't expect an AI to fully understand your code. It can't. Ask someone who actually knows and understands C++: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask
